english: Let $S_0$ be the sphere $x^2+y^2+z^2=18$ and let $C$ be the circle in which $S_0$ meets the plane $x+2y+2z=9$. Let $L$ be the line $x=-1,\ y+3=z-2$. There are exactly two spheres each of which contains the circle $C$ and touches the line $L$. Then the radius of the smaller of these two spheres is
hindi: माना $S_0$ गोला $x^2+y^2+z^2=18$ है तथा $C$ वह वृत्त है जिसमें $S_0$ समतल $x+2y+2z=9$ से मिलता है। माना $L$ रेखा $x=-1,\ y+3=z-2$ है। ठीक दो गोले ऐसे हैं जिनमें से प्रत्येक वृत्त $C$ को समाहित करता है तथा रेखा $L$ को स्पर्श करता है। तब इन दोनों गोलों में से छोटे गोले की त्रिज्या है
solution: Distance of $O$ from the plane $=\dfrac93=3$: $C$ has centre $N(1,2,2)$ (foot of the perpendicular from $O$) and radius $\sqrt{18-9}=3$
A sphere containing $C$ has its centre on the normal to the plane through $N$: $K=(1+\lambda,2+2\lambda,2+2\lambda)$, $R^2=9+NK^2=9+9\lambda^2$
solution_full: The distance of the centre $O$ of $S_0$ from the plane $x+2y+2z=9$ is $\dfrac{9}{\sqrt{1+4+4}}=3<3\sqrt2$, so the plane cuts $S_0$ in a circle.
The centre of $C$ is the foot $N$ of the perpendicular from $O$ to the plane: $N=\dfrac{9}{9}(1,2,2)=(1,2,2)$; its radius is $\sqrt{18-9}=3$.

Every point of $C$ is at distance $3$ from $N$ in the plane, so a point $K$ is equidistant from all points of $C$ exactly when $K$ lies on the line through $N$ perpendicular to the plane. So the centre of a sphere containing $C$ is $K=(1+\lambda,\,2+2\lambda,\,2+2\lambda)$, and its radius satisfies $R^2=NK^2+3^2=9\lambda^2+9$.
The line $L$ passes through $A(-1,-3,2)$ with direction $\overrightarrow{e}=(0,1,1)$, $|\overrightarrow{e}|=\sqrt2$.
The sphere touches $L$ when $d=R$: $25+2(4+4\lambda+\lambda^2)=18+18\lambda^2$, i.e. $16\lambda^2-8\lambda-15=0$, so $\lambda=\dfrac{8\pm32}{32}$: $\lambda=\dfrac54$ or $\lambda=-\dfrac34$.

$\lambda=\dfrac54$: $R^2=9+9\cdot\dfrac{25}{16}=\dfrac{369}{16}$, $R=\dfrac{3\sqrt{41}}{4}$. ($S_0$ itself, $\lambda=-1$, does not touch $L$: its centre is at distance $\sqrt{\frac{27}{2}}$ from $L$, not $3\sqrt2$.)
originality_note: New: the spheres through a fixed circle form a one-parameter family with centres on the normal through the circle centre, and the member is fixed by tangency to a line (way 3: a family with a second condition). Closest known: the sphere through the circle S + lambda P = 0 that touches a given plane, or passes through a point. Different because: tangency to a line (point-line distance) replaces tangency to a plane, giving a quadratic with two genuine spheres to compare.

concept_use.Sphere in three dimensions: The circle C (centre N, radius 3) as a section of S_0, and every sphere through C has centre K on the normal at N with R^2 = 9 + NK^2.
concept_use.Line and a plane: The foot of the perpendicular from O to the plane gives N, the centre line is the normal to the plane through N, and the tangency condition is the distance of K from the line L.

stem_review: Read as a student: every point, line and plane is introduced before use, every condition is stated, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed independently with sympy and numpy, is unique and equals the Answer Plan; the options have one form and exactly one is correct. Checked that the plane cuts S_0, that S_0 itself does not touch L (so exactly two spheres), and that 'smaller' picks one of them. Changed: altered the sphere from radius 5 to radius 3 sqrt 2 so that no option equals the radius of S_0 by coincidence.
key_step: Recognising that the centres of spheres through C lie on the normal at N with R^2 = 9 + NK^2, then the tangency to L as a point-line distance.
justification: Two linked ideas (family of spheres through a circle, distance of a point from a line) and a quadratic; typical average Advanced 3D work. Comparable with 2023-P1-Q16 (L3) and 2026-P1-Q6 (L3).
